title: Conditional Probability and Independence
seo_title: Conditional Probability Worksheet: Independence and Two-Way Tables (Geometry, S-CP) | 100 Questions
standard_text: Understand the conditional probability of A given B as P(A and B)/P(B), and interpret independence of A and B as saying that the conditional probability of A given B is the same as the probability of A, and the conditional probability of B given A is the same as the probability of B.
meta_desc: Free worksheet on conditional probability: the Addition Rule, independent events, P(B | A), two-way tables and drawing without replacement. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: P(B | A) = P(A and B) ÷ P(A).
key_sub: Independent events: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B). Without replacement, the total goes down.
body_html:
How it works

  • Complement: P(not A) = 1 − P(A).
  • Addition Rule: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B). Subtract the overlap so it is not counted twice.
  • Conditional probability: P(B | A) means the probability of B given A. P(B | A) = P(A and B) ÷ P(A). In a two-way table, use only the row or column you are given.
  • Independent events do not affect each other: P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B), and P(B | A) = P(B).

Drawing without replacement changes the second probability, because one item is gone.

Example

P(A) = 0.5, P(B) = 0.4 and P(A and B) = 0.2. Are A and B independent?

0.5 × 0.4 = 0.2

This equals P(A and B)

Answer: Yes

Example

A bag has 3 red and 2 blue marbles. Two are drawn without replacement. Find P(both red).

3/5 × 2/4

Answer: 3/10

Common mistakes

  • Adding P(A) and P(B) without subtracting P(A and B).
  • Dividing by the grand total when the question says "given". Divide by the row or column total.
  • Mixing up P(A | B) and P(B | A).
  • Keeping the same total for the second draw without replacement.

faq.a: The probability of an event given that another event has happened. P(B | A) = P(A and B) ÷ P(A).

faq.q: How do you know if two events are independent?
faq.a: Check whether P(A and B) = P(A) × P(B), or whether P(B | A) = P(B). If so, they are independent.

faq.q: What is the Addition Rule in probability?
faq.a: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B). For mutually exclusive events, P(A and B) = 0.

faq.q: How do you find a conditional probability from a two-way table?
faq.a: Use only the row or column for the given condition, and divide the cell count by that row or column total.

items.e: Outcomes 1, 2 and 6: 3/6 = 12. These events cannot happen together.

items.q: A bag has 6 green marbles and 3 yellow marbles. Two are drawn without replacement. What is the probability the first is green and the second is yellow?

items.e: With replacement the draws are independent: 37 × 37 = 949.

items.q: A bag has 6 black marbles and 5 white marbles. Mateo takes two marbles without replacement. What is the probability both are black?
items.e: First black: 6/11. One black is gone, so the second is 5/10. 611 × 12 = 311.
